newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania issues incentives for foreign share buyers.
newsitem.headline: Romania issues incentives for foreign share buyers.

text.p: Romania on Monday began offering lower taxes on profits and exemption from customs duty to foreign investors buying stakes in state companies.
A government decree on foreign investment, which became effective on publication in the official gazette, is seen as a way to step up privatisation by involving foreign capital inflows in selloffs.

Foreign investors buying into Romanian companies will pay a 15 percent tax on their gross profit in the first five years after signing a contract with the State Ownership Fund (FPS), which has a controlling stake in most Romanian companies.
Profit tax in Romania is currently 38 percent.
This and other incentives apply to foreigners who buy a package of at least $1 million, its equivalent in other currencies or in the domestic leu currency, the decree said.
Privatisation was slow in the seven years of leftist rule from the 1989 collapse of communism to last November's centrist victory in parliamentary and presidential elections.
The new government has pledged to step up selloffs of state companies under a tough reform package launched in February.
Shortage of domestic capital and thin interest from foreign investors have frequently been quoted as reasons for delays.
At end-1996 Romania had privatised fewer than half the more than 6,500 firms slated for selloff when the process started.

The decree also provides for an eight-year exemption from duties and value added tax (VAT) for installations and equipment needed for upgrading or environmental protection. An additional two-year 50-percent reduction is also available.
Romania charges a uniform 18 percent VAT, with some exceptions, where the level is nine percent.
Know-how transfers are also exempt from customs duties and there is a four-year 50-percent cut in raw materials and spare parts import duties.
Buyers of Romanian company stakes are also entitled to 60 percent of the sale proceeds, which return to the company to step up the privatisation process.
